newsitem.title: FRANCE: French finance ministry denies Arthuis resigning.
newsitem.headline: French finance ministry denies Arthuis resigning.

text.p: The French finance ministry denied on Thursday market talk that Finance Minister Jean Arthuis might be about to resign.
"We formally deny any resignation rumours," a finance ministry spokeswoman said.

At Prime Minister Alain Juppe's office, an official repeated a denial made on Wednesday that a government reshuffle was not being prepared. A reshuffle "is really not the priority at the moment," she said.
Official sources said on Wednesday that any reshuffle would probably not be until early next year rather than this year.
Talk of a reshuffle had fuelled market rumours that Arthuis might be forced to step down to pave the way for an ally of former prime minister Edouard Balladur to take over the finance ministry.

A reshuffle has been seen by some as one way of healing a rift inside the RPR party, the senior partner in the government coalition, caused by a decision by Balladur to run against fellow RPR member President Jacques Chirac in France's presidential elections in 1995.
